speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if it started as a blister or a bite?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ecthyma gangrenosum secondary to diabetic foot infection (Pseudomonas aeruginosa).

The patient has significant risk factors including diabetes and a history of uveitis treated with steroids, which predisposes her to severe soft tissue infections. The progression from a bite site to a painful ulcer over one month is highly concerning for a necrotizing infection. I will proceed with wound culture and blood cultures to confirm the pathogen.
